title: Media player
summary: This machine controls the audio player in a phone app. It decides when the player plays, stops, and waits.
context: A user selects a track. Then the player loads the track and plays it.
A phone call can stop the audio. After the call, the player goes back to the step it was in before the call.

glossary.definition: One audio file, for example one song.
To load part of a track into memory before the player plays it.
To set the sound to zero. The track continues to play.

stopped.meaning: The player does not play. It can load a track.

active.meaning: The player has a track. Two parts work at the same time: the playback and the volume.

playback.meaning: This part controls the position in the track.

playback_last.meaning: This marker remembers the last playback state. A return to it goes back to that state.

buffering.meaning: The player loads the start of the track into memory.

paused.meaning: The track stops at the current position. The position does not change.

ended.meaning: The track is at its end.

volume.meaning: This part controls the sound level.

unmuted.meaning: The user can hear the sound.

interrupted.meaning: A phone call stopped the audio.

finished.meaning: The track is complete. The player goes back to the stopped state at once.

player.play.meaning: The user pushes the play button.

player.pause.meaning: The user pushes the pause button.

player.stop.meaning: The user pushes the stop button.

player.reset.meaning: The player clears the completed track.
player.reset.origin: The machine sends this event to itself.

track.end.meaning: The audio file has no more sound.
track.end.origin: The audio system of the phone.

volume.toggle.meaning: The user pushes the mute button.

hasTrack.meaning: The player has a track in memory.

t-load.meaning: The player keeps the track. The state does not change.

t-play.meaning: If the player has a track, the playback and the volume parts start.

t-stop.meaning: From each active state, the user can stop the player.

t-call.meaning: A phone call stops the audio. The player remembers the playback state.

t-history-default.meaning: If the player has no record of a playback state, it starts again at the buffer step.

t-finish.meaning: When the playback part ends, the player leaves the active state.

t-buffered.meaning: When the track is in memory, the track starts to play. No event is necessary.

t-pause.meaning: The track stops at the current position.

t-end.meaning: The track has no more sound.

t-resume.meaning: The track plays again from the same position.

t-call-end.meaning: After the call, the player goes back to the last playback state.

t-reset.meaning: The player goes back to the stopped state.

scenarios.name: Play a track to the end
scenarios.goal: Show the normal path of one track.

steps.caption: The user selects a track. The player keeps it.
The player loads the start of the track. Then the track plays.
The user mutes the sound. The track continues to play.
The track ends. The player stops and clears the track.

scenarios.name: A phone call during a pause
scenarios.goal: Show how the player remembers its last state.

steps.caption: The user stops the track for a short time.
A phone call starts. The player remembers that it was in pause.
The call ends. The player goes back to the pause, not to the start.
The user plays the track again from the same position.
The user turns the sound on again.

evidence.note: The `mode` field and the `isMuted` flag change together in each handler.

notes.title: Volume after a call
notes.text: The history marker records only the playback part. The volume part starts again as `unmuted` after each call.
